notes: The uninstaller did not work. Its shortcut sweep was one PowerShell block with the pipes written as ^| -- which is how a pipe is escaped on a cmd command line, but not inside a quoted string, where the caret is just a caret. PowerShell was handed a literal ^| , refused to parse the whole block, printed a parser error and carried on, so every Desktop, Startup and Start menu shortcut survived an uninstall that said it had removed them. And the app folder was left to a copy in %TEMP% that only started once the window had closed, so nothing could report whether it had gone -- and when the radio was still open it silently could not go, because the shortcut makes that folder the browser's working directory and Windows will not delete a folder something is running in. The handover now happens first instead: the folder is removed in a window that is still there to say so, and to say why in those words if it cannot. A shortcut is also no longer removed on its name alone unless what it points at is gone, so uninstalling one copy stops taking another copy's Start menu entry with it.
